Ravi: Quick sync: prototype for the usage dashboard toolbar — thinking about two patterns: 1) a persistent left rail that contains the org/project toggle + date range + quick download, or 2) a compact top bar over the chart with an overflow menu for download. Which is better for discoverability and accessibility? Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abc (page 'Usage Toolbar variants'). Lina: I prefer the left rail for large-screen density. It keeps controls visually grouped and means the chart area doesn't shift when users change filters. But mobile gets cramped; we'd collapse the rail into a top bar on small breakpoints. Jules: Left rail is fine, but it increases visual weight. If we go rail, use a subtle divider and allow collapsing. Also, if we keep the invoice download in the rail it's very discoverable, but makes the rail a mixed-controls area (filters + actions). My vote: put filters top-left, actions (download, export) top-right in the header, so they read as separate concerns. Eli: Implementation notes: our current chart library doesn't like width jitter. If toggle is in the header and changes chart granularity (org vs project) we need to debounce re-layouts. If it's a rail that doesn't change chart width, less reflow. Also for invoices, CSV is cheap; PDF adds a job. Backend can return a signed URL for either. Ravi: Good point on reflow. So maybe a hybrid: filters (org/project toggle + date) in the rail, actions (Download caret, Export options) in header. That preserves discoverability and reduces chart jitter. Lina: Copy nit: the token breakdown label currently shows "Tokens" and a small percentage. People outside infra confuse tokens with usage minutes. Suggest label "Token units (input+output)" with tooltip: "Tokens count both request and response tokens. See docs." Tooltip should be keyboard accessible. Jules: For the chart legend, can we show both absolute tokens and token-cost (USD) toggles? Some customers want economical context not raw tokens. Toggle could be small pill next to legend. Eli: We'll need to convert tokens -> USD using model pricing. That's fine but watch rounding noise. Backend can supply both metrics in the same payload to avoid client math. Ravi: Accessibility checks: a11y-bot can you run contrast and semantics on both variants? Also ensure the download menu is reachable by keyboard and announces options via ARIA. a11y-bot: queued accessibility scan for branch feature/usage-toolbar-variant. Preliminary: header-action buttons pass contrast, left-rail text fails at smaller sizes, download menu lacks aria-haspopup on the toggle, chart SVG missing for screen readers. Report: https://ci.redwood.ai/a11y/609. Lina: For keyboard: when focus lands on the org/project toggle, arrow keys should switch options, and Enter should apply change. Focus must not jump to the chart. Also, when a download starts, we should show a non-modal toast with link to the file and keyboard focus on toast's dismiss. Jules: Data-density: collapsed project lists should show top 5 projects by spend + a "Show all" row that expands. Avoid rendering >50 rows at once. Use virtualization for the expanded view. Telemetry: track expand, download format chosen, and toggle frequency. Eli: Sample ARIA snippet for download menu: ```html
``` Ravi: Good. Also small accessibility contrast decision: avoid thin gray dividers; use 2px solid at low contrast or a softened shadow to separate rail from canvas. Lina: Invoice copy: instead of "Download invoice" use "Download invoice (selected scope)" and then the caret for format. That makes it explicit. For confusion reduction, put current scope (Org: Acme Corp / Project: web) in the button tooltip. Jules: UX edge-case: when a user has both org and project selected (multi-project view), what does "Download (CSV)" mean — full rollup or per-project rows? Suggest default to rollup CSV with an option in the menu "Download per-project CSV". Eli: Backend: we'll implement two endpoints: /invoices/rollup.csv and /invoices/per-project.csv; we can make the per-project option streamable to avoid timeouts. We'll also tag downloads with request_id for telemetry. Ravi: Final checklist from this thread: 1) Hybrid layout: filters in left rail, actions in header. 2) Download button as header action with caret menu (CSV default, PDF option, per-project submenu). 3) Token label clarification + tooltip. 4) Accessibility fixes: in chart SVG, aria-haspopup, keyboard menu + toast focus handling, contrast updates. 5) Perf: top-N + Show all + virtualization. 6) Telemetry for toggles/downloads/expands. Owners: Lina (copy + a11y copy), Jules (UX edge cases + telemetry), Eli (backend endpoints + perf), Ravi (design sign-off). Lina: I'll update Figma and add the tooltip copy and keyboard states. Jules: I'll draft the telemetry events and the export UX microcopy. Eli: Starting backend endpoints in the morning; will coordinate expected payload shape with frontend. Ravi: Thanks team. We'll review the staging preview in tomorrow's demo slot. :white_check_mark:
